extraction.identifier_query: Does the current article explicitly state a Curie temperature (Curie point, Tc, or T_C) for at least one identifiable material composition? Include current-work, background, comparison, and cited-material statements when the article makes the material-to-Tc relationship explicit. Answer 'yes' or 'no' with a single word. Do not count ambiguous material-value relationships or temperatures that are clearly synthesis/annealing/sintering/measurement/Néel/blocking/glass transition/decomposition temperatures. A Tm or dielectric peak qualifies only when its local context explicitly identifies a normal Curie or ferroelectric-to-paraelectric transition; exclude frequency-dependent relaxor peaks and generic dielectric maxima.
extraction.extraction_instructions:
['You are extracting the Curie temperature (Tc / T_C / Curie point) reported for each material composition, not any other temperature.', "Do not treat 'Tc' as Curie temperature unless the surrounding context explicitly identifies it as Curie temperature / Curie point.", "Keep the exact composition -> Curie temperature mapping. Do not assign one composition's Tc to another composition.", 'If multiple compositions or doping levels are studied, treat them as distinct compositions and preserve their own Tc values.', 'Do not invent, estimate, or calculate a Tc value from external knowledge.']
['Extract the Curie temperature explicitly stated for each identifiable material composition in the current article.', "If variable composition values are explicitly reported, preserve them so the existing MaterialParserTool variable-composition normalization can operate later. Example: 'Bi(1-x)NdxFeO3 where x=0.05'.", 'Do NOT extract temperatures that are clearly synthesis temperatures, annealing temperatures, sintering temperatures, measurement temperatures, Néel temperatures, blocking temperatures, glass transition temperatures, decomposition temperatures, or generic phase-transition temperatures unless the article explicitly identifies the value as Curie temperature / Curie point / Tc in the relevant context.', 'If the article does not provide a Curie temperature for a composition, do not invent one and do not use external scientific knowledge.', "Preserve the reported unit exactly. Use 'K' or '°C' as reported; do not silently convert between units.", 'ARTICLE SCOPE: Extract every material-to-Curie-temperature fact explicitly asserted by the article. This includes current-work samples, background or comparison materials, and facts attributed to cited publications. Do not use external knowledge or invent a relationship that the article does not state.', "TC SEMANTICS: Treat an explicitly assigned Curie transition, normal ferroelectric-to-paraelectric transition, or loss of long-range ferroelectric order as Curie-temperature evidence. Exclude relaxor peak temperatures, dipole-glass transitions, frequency-dependent Tm values, and unrelated dielectric maxima. When normal and relaxor samples coexist, extract only each material's locally supported normal Curie/FE-PE facts.", 'BINDING: Bind every value to the exact material that the article associates with it. A constituent background fact may be extracted for that constituent, but must not be transferred to a composite. Likewise, keep a measured composite value bound to the composite rather than substituting a constituent.', 'FINAL CHECK: For every proposed record, confirm that the article explicitly asserts the target transition and exact material-value binding. Remove the record if either check fails.']
